title: Scaling the obsolescence scanner to the whole org
subtitle: Why throughput is the constraint, and the plan to lift it tenfold

title: What limits throughput
subtitle: One worker, three minutes a scan

title: Three quarters of scan time is spent waiting on the database

items.label: of each scan is database wait

items.heading: Queries run one at a time
items.text: Each dependency lookup waits for the previous one to return.

items.heading: No connection pooling
items.text: Every scan opens and closes its own connection.

items.heading: Matching is CPU-light
items.text: The matching engine itself takes under 20 seconds per scan.

title: Four options were weighed; the worker pool wins on cost and risk

items.heading: Worker pool
items.text: Run 16 scans in parallel on the existing service.

items.heading: Query batching
items.text: Batch dependency lookups into one round trip.

items.heading: Bigger database
items.text: Scale the instance up; costs double.

items.heading: Rewrite engine
items.text: Six months of work with uncertain gains.

title: The pool changes how scans run, not what they find

columns.label: Today
points: One worker takes scans in arrival order
A slow scan blocks every scan behind it
Throughput is capped at 20 an hour

columns.label: With the pool
points: A slow scan holds up only its own worker
Throughput scales until the database is the limit

title: Rollout takes one quarter, with a checkpoint every month

items.heading: Pool of 4
items.text: Behind a flag, on one business unit.

items.heading: Pool of 8
items.text: All units; database metrics watched daily.

items.heading: Target met
items.text: 200+ scans an hour, sustained for two weeks.

items.label: Decision
items.text: Approve the pool of 4 pilot for next sprint.

title: Cost grows linearly while throughput grows tenfold
footnote: Costs include compute and the database read replica.

title: What the review board asked us to keep in mind

items.text: Throughput is a means; the goal is that no team waits more than a day to learn which of its dependencies are obsolete.

title: Most quick wins are in the database, not the engine
Throughput climbs with each pool size until the database saturates

items.text: Pool of 4 went live in October.
Pool of 8 doubled it in November.
December's pool of 16 is near the database ceiling.
